version.changelog: Security: Removed cron integration (contradicted session-only claim). Removed agent step examples that implied undeclared integrations. Clarified limitations.

llm.summary: The skill's requests and instructions are coherent with its purpose (planning and simulating short workflows); it asks for no credentials or installs and is instruction-only.

dimensions.detail: The name/description (build and simulate multi-step workflows) aligns with the runtime instructions. The skill is instruction-only, requires no binaries, env vars, or installs — which is reasonable for a planner/simulator. Minor inconsistency: the registry metadata listed no homepage while the SKILL.md includes a homepage URL (small metadata mismatch).
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md limits workflows to the session and states no files are read/written and exec steps are not run — this keeps scope narrow. It does instruct the agent to use built-in HTTP capabilities to perform API steps and to 'perform the action directly using built-in tools', which is expected for chaining API calls but gives the agent discretion to contact external endpoints specified in a workflow. Users should be aware that workflows can make arbitrary outbound HTTP requests if the user defines such steps.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec or code files are present (instruction-only). Nothing is written to disk by an installer, so install risk is minimal.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: No environment variables, credentials, or config paths are requested. This is proportionate for a session-only workflow planner. Note: if a user includes API steps that require credentials, those credentials would need to be provided at runtime by the user (not requested by the skill itself).
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill does not request persistent presence (always is false) and explicitly states workflows are ephemeral and not persisted. It does not modify other skills or system config according to the provided instructions.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to do what it says: design and simulate short, session-only workflows. Before using it: avoid embedding secrets (API keys, passwords, tokens) directly in workflow steps; be cautious when adding API steps that call external endpoints (those calls can send data out); use the dry-run feature to verify behavior before executing; if you need to integrate with real services, prefer a vetted connector (e.g., the referenced smart-api-connector) and provide only the minimal credentials required. If you require guarantees about where request logs are kept or how session data is stored, ask the publisher or platform for details about the agent's built-in HTTP tool and session handling.
